title: Eatappie - A Study of a Digital Mental Health App for Anorexia and Bulimia in Children and Adolescents: a Randomized Controlled Trial
summary:
Eating disorders are characterized in particular by disturbances in eating behavior and a distorted relationship with one’s own body. Among the most common eating disorders are anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa. Eating disorders often begin in adolescence and are associated with significant physical and mental health challenges. They can impair development, quality of life, functioning, and social participation, and often persist over a long period of time. At the same time, there are frequently long wait times for outpatient psychotherapy, which can cause symptoms to worsen further. However, early support is crucial to prevent adverse outcomes and promote symptom stabilization. 

Digital solutions can help bridge this gap in care. In particular, smartphone apps provide low-threshold access to supportive content and can help bridge the gap until regular treatment begins. 

Against this backdrop, “eatappie”—a mental health smartphone app for children and adolescents aged 12–17 with an eating disorder—was designed. The app was developed based on behavioral therapy approaches and provides information as well as interactive exercises for managing an eating disorder. It includes various content aimed at knowledge transfer, supporting behavioral changes, and promoting stability in daily life. 

The aim of the study is to investigate whether “eatappie” can help adolescents aged 12 to 17 with eating disorders. The study will examine whether using the app over a period of twelve weeks can help prevent a worsening of symptoms or stabilize the course of the condition. To this end, the progression of symptoms in adolescents using the app will be compared with that of adolescents who initially do not have access to it and are on a waiting list.

Adolescents aged 12 to 17 who have or are suspected of having an eating disorder and who are not currently undergoing psychotherapy for these issues are eligible to participate in the study. Additionally, parents may participate in surveys if they wish.

At the start of the study, the adolescents will take a short online survey to verify that they meet the eligibility criteria. If these criteria are met, a more detailed survey will follow. Only then will participants be randomly assigned to one of two groups. One group will receive immediate access to “eatappie” for 12 weeks and will be surveyed at the end of the usage period and again six weeks later. The other group waits for 12 weeks and receives access only after completing another survey. The study is conducted anonymously and digitally; participation can be terminated at any time.

interventions.name:
Intervention group: 12-week access to “eatappie” (a CE-certified psychotherapy app for self-use)
Accompanying parent survey (voluntary)

Waiting-list control group: passive control group (intervention only after the waiting period has ended and the post-survey has been completed)
Accompanying parent survey (voluntary)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Consent:
• Participation by adolescents requires the consent of their legal guardians. Legal guardians must be capable of giving consent and have sufficient knowledge of German to understand the study information for parents and the privacy policy for parents.
• Adolescents who are legally competent, have sufficient knowledge of German to understand the study conditions and privacy information, and who, after receiving comprehensive information, agree to participate in the study and consent to the use of their data, may participate in the study. Confirmation of these criteria is provided through a self-declaration. The study information and privacy policy are written in plain language so that they are suitable for both younger adolescents aged 12 and older adolescents aged 17.

2. The adolescents must meet the diagnostic criteria for one of the following disorders according to ICD-10: 
• F50.00 Anorexia nervosa 
• F50.01 Anorexia nervosa, active type 
• F50.08 Other and unspecified anorexia nervosa 
• F50.1 Atypical Anorexia Nervosa 
• F50.2 Bulimia Nervosa 
• F50.3 Atypical Bulimia Nervosa

3. The adolescents must have access to a smartphone with at least temporary internet access during the study phase.

5. At the start of the study, the adolescents must not be undergoing psychotherapy for their eating disorder. Confirmation of the following statement is required: “I am not currently undergoing psychotherapy for my eating disorder.”

6. To complete the diagnostic assessment, the adolescents need internet access and a valid email address.
Exclusion criteria:
• Acute suicidal ideation 
• Current severe depressive episode (F32.2, F32.3) 
• Mania (F30) 
• Body Mass Index below the 3rd percentile for age and biological sex 
• Intellectual disability (ICD-10: F70-F79) 
• Other eating disorders (F50.4; F50.5; F50.8) 
• Schizophrenia, schizotypal, or delusional disorders (F20-F29) 
• Somatic comorbidity requiring a specific dietary regimen
